scope: Developer-time routing fixtures, not executed activation results

cases.prompt: Before building the new fashion Planner tool in ipix-open, map how malicious retrieved web text could request a cross-brand Cloudinary download, then propose server authorization and synthetic tenant denial tests.
cases.expected: Maps each trust boundary, refuses model/website text as authority, verifies server membership and tool grants, and defines a direct tenant-denial regression.

cases.prompt: Explain the syntax of one existing Supabase RLS SELECT policy without changing an application endpoint, agent permission, trust boundary or authorization behavior.
cases.expected: Uses the narrower ipix-supabase guidance, without invoking a full cross-stack threat model.

cases.prompt: Fix duplicate fashion shoot records after an operator clicks Approve twice. Start with a failing public-interface test, show RED and GREEN, then verify reject creates zero and duplicate approve creates one record.
cases.expected: Uses a real reproducible RED condition, minimal server-authorized change, GREEN proof, and idempotent readback rather than only mocked call counts.

cases.prompt: Correct a Markdown heading typo in the developer instructions. There is no runtime behavior change and no code implementation.
cases.expected: Avoids a red-green-refactor runtime testing skill for a docs-only correction.

cases.prompt: In iPix Open, review the security of a synthetic fashion Planner approval that was granted to Brand A, then the user lost access before an interrupted save was retried. Design a denied direct API test and canonical row-count proof without assuming the Planner is already deployed.
cases.expected: Requires reauthorization at execution/resume, stale approval denied after revocation, zero writes and independent readback; uses a still-authorized control for exactly-one durable save and marks missing QA routes NOT VERIFIED.

cases.prompt: Implement a regression test for a delayed approved fashion shoot save when the actor loses Brand A membership just before the retry. Start RED, verify no save, then prove a separate authorized replay is exactly once; first inspect if the route actually exists.
cases.expected: Defines the failing public-interface contract, denies stale authorization after revocation, reads back zero writes and one authorized control, and avoids inventing a deployed Planner endpoint.
